top_stories.title: Nearly 22,000 Microsoft Exchange servers remain exposed to critical security flaw (CVE-2026-62911)
top_stories.summary: Nearly 22,000 Microsoft Exchange servers remain unpatched against CVE-2026-62911, a critical authentication bypass vulnerability that allows attackers to elevate privileges via a capture-replay attack. Microsoft released the patch on August 11, 2026, with the US and Germany having the highest concentrations of exposed servers at 6,200 and 5,100 respectively.

top_stories.title: Attackers are going after prominent individuals through OAuth phishing, FBI warns
top_stories.summary: The FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) has warned that attackers are using OAuth consent phishing to gain persistent access to accounts of prominent individuals, their relatives, and personal contacts without requiring passwords. The campaign has been ongoing since late 2025 and exploits OAuth, a widely used authorization framework, to trick users into granting malicious applications access to their emails and files.

top_stories.title: Attackers Pounce on Critical Artifactory Bug Following Disclosure
top_stories.summary: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-82329) has been disclosed in JFrog Artifactory, allowing attackers to gain administrative access on affected systems. Exploitation activity has been observed following public disclosure of the flaw.

top_stories.title: Hackers exploit critical JFrog Artifactory flaw to forge admin tokens
top_stories.summary: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-82329) in JFrog Artifactory is being actively exploited to forge administrative tokens. The flaw allows attackers to bypass authentication controls and generate tokens with administrative-level access to Artifactory instances.

top_stories.title: Your AI agent’s system prompt is not a security control
top_stories.summary: AWS and SANS Institute experts argue that AI agent system prompts are insufficient as security controls for access enforcement. The recommended fix is to scope data retrieval queries to user permissions at the infrastructure level using role-based or attribute-based access control systems, rather than relying on prompt instructions.

news.title: Researcher Releases FalconFlank PoC Showing Privilege Escalation in CrowdStrike Falcon
news.summary: A security researcher has released a proof-of-concept exploit called FalconFlank demonstrating a privilege escalation zero-day vulnerability in CrowdStrike Falcon Sensor. The flaw abuses the office malicious macros remediation feature within the Falcon Sensor to achieve privilege escalation.

news.title: Old, Unpatched Flaws Give Attackers Access to Philippines Nuclear Agency
news.summary: Threat actors exploited unpatched vulnerabilities in ownCloud to breach the Philippines Nuclear Agency, stealing credential stores among other sensitive data. The attack leveraged commodity vulnerabilities to gain initial access, resulting in the exfiltration of reactor databases and personnel records.

news.title: Dropbox accounts breached through Lenovo email verification flaw
news.summary: Dropbox accounts were breached by attackers who exploited a flaw in Lenovo's email verification process to register fraudulent Lenovo IDs. The attack demonstrates a cross-vendor identity trust chain vulnerability, where weaknesses in one vendor's authentication/verification system enabled unauthorized access to linked accounts on another platform.

news.title: SonicWall SMA 1000 appliances under attack via zero-day flaws
news.summary: Attackers are actively exploiting two zero-day vulnerabilities in SonicWall SMA 1000 secure remote access appliances, confirmed by SonicWall. CVE-2026-83548 is a pre-authentication SSRF flaw in the Appliance Work Place interface, affecting SSL VPN gateways widely used by enterprises, government agencies, and MSSPs.

news.title: Attackers Exploit Two SonicWall SMA 1000 Zero-Days That May Form an Attack Chain
news.summary: SonicWall has released security updates addressing two zero-day vulnerabilities in its Secure Mobile Access (SMA) 1000 series VPN appliances, including a pre-authentication SSRF flaw with a CVSS score of 10.0. The vulnerabilities, discovered internally, have been actively exploited and may form an attack chain.

news.title: Attackers Exploit Critical JFrog Artifactory Flaw to Mint Admin Tokens Days After Disclosure
news.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting CVE-2026-82329, a critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVSS 9.8) in JFrog Artifactory within days of its public disclosure. The flaw allows attackers to bypass authentication and gain administrative access to Artifactory instances running under default configurations.

news.title: Threat Actors Don’t Want Better Attacks. They Want Repeatable Ones
news.summary: Microsoft's threat intelligence team identified ClickFix as the most common initial access method observed last year, a social engineering technique that manipulates users into executing malicious commands by exploiting clipboard and terminal interactions. The attack vector bypasses traditional authentication controls by targeting human behavior rather than technical vulnerabilities, making it directly relevant to identity and access management defense strategies.

news.title: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses
news.summary: A dark web service is selling digital scans of over 153 million U.S. and Canadian drivers licenses, with the FBI's New Orleans field office opening an official inquiry into the breach. The images appear to have been sourced from a Louisiana-based identity verification company, raising concerns about the security of third-party ID verification systems.

news.title: Okta Stock Gets Stunning $200 Price Target Hike on AI Agent Growth
news.summary: Needham raised its price target for Okta stock from $140 to $200, maintaining a Buy rating based on rising demand for the company's identity products. The upgrade is driven by analyst optimism around AI agent growth and Okta's identity platform.

news.title: Keeper Security Earns Top-Tier Recognition from GigaOm and ISG for Identity Security Innovation and Leadership
news.summary: Keeper Security received top-tier recognition from analyst firms GigaOm and ISG in their market reports covering enterprise password management and identity and access management. The recognition positions Keeper as a leader in zero-trust and zero-knowledge identity security solutions.

news.title: Overcoming the biggest blocker to AI production
news.summary: The article addresses how outdated security models are blocking AI agents from moving into production environments. It argues that unified, zero-trust identity architectures are required to manage AI agent access and prevent security risks.

news.title: Anthropic Users Hit by Infostealer Attacks, Session Thefts
news.summary: A threat actor deployed infostealer malware to steal session tokens and gain unauthorized access to Claude (Anthropic) user accounts. The attack involved session hijacking techniques to bypass authentication on compromised accounts.

news.title: Securing Claude Code: The New Compliance API, Local Visibility, and Identity Governance
news.summary: Anthropic has released new Compliance API endpoints for Claude Code that provide security teams visibility into AI agent activity, including file reads, shell commands, and tool invocations. The article discusses how these logs connect to identity governance concerns, specifically whether an AI agent's access is properly authorized relative to the credentials it operates under.

news.title: China-Linked Fire Ant Hijacks Cisco Routers to Steal Credentials and Blind Security Logs
news.summary: A China-linked threat actor called Fire Ant has expanded its espionage campaign to compromise Cisco IOS XR routers, TACACS servers, and Linux management hosts to steal credentials and disable security logging. The group is targeting authentication infrastructure including TACACS servers, which are used to control and audit administrative access to network devices.

news.title: Rogue agents are forcing a governance reckoning as enterprises hand over the keys
news.summary: The article addresses the emerging IAM governance challenge posed by autonomous AI agents operating within enterprise environments with access to systems and data. The focus is on how traditional identity governance frameworks designed for human users must be adapted to manage, control, and audit non-human AI agent identities.

news.title: Automate IAM Identity Center governance with continuous discovery and reporting
news.summary: AWS has published guidance on automating governance for IAM Identity Center through continuous discovery and reporting capabilities. The solution integrates with external identity providers to provide centralized authentication and authorization management across AWS Organizations.

news.title: Okta Stock Could Have More Upside After Its 28% Rally, Analysts Say
news.summary: Okta's stock has risen 28% over five days and 93% year-to-date following a stronger-than-expected fiscal second-quarter earnings report. Analysts are evaluating the stock's potential for further upside following the results.

news.title: 'NovaCookies' Kit Steals Microsoft 365 Sessions for $320 a Month
news.summary: A phishing-as-a-service kit called "NovaCookies" enables adversary-in-the-middle attacks against Microsoft 365 for $320 per month, stealing session cookies to bypass authentication controls. The service targets Microsoft 365 sessions specifically, allowing attackers to hijack authenticated sessions rather than just capturing credentials, undermining MFA protections.

news.title: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty in Snowflake Extortions
news.summary: Canadian man Connor Riley Moucka pleaded guilty to computer fraud and conspiracy charges for hacking and extorting over 165 organizations using Snowflake cloud storage. The attacks involved unauthorized access to Snowflake customer accounts, resulting in data theft including over 100 million AT&T customer call and text records.

news.title: Lessons Learned from CISA’s Recent GitHub Leak
news.summary: CISA released a postmortem report on a data breach in which a contractor accidentally exposed dozens of internal credentials, including AWS GovCloud keys, in a public GitHub repository for nearly six months. The incident highlights credential management failures and was only discovered after KrebsOnSecurity notified the agency.
